Interested in a new Senior Network Engineer opportunity?   
  Your new company  
 By joining the Queensland Government, you are joining a dynamic team committed to shaping and elevating Queensland's workforce to meet the evolving needs of our industries, ensuring prosperity and agility in our economic landscape. 
   
  Your new role   
 As a Senior Network Specialist within the Public Safety Network Centre (PSNMC) Deployment team, you will be crucial in the support of deploying network capabilities for the supported agencies. You will be responsible for configuring hardware for deployment, commission hardware for sites and the implementation of the project deliverables. 
   
  Key Responsibilities   
 As the Senior Network Specialist, you will: 
 
 
 Build and configure Cisco routers according to network specifications for operation within an SR-MPLS framework. 
 
 
 Update inventory and configuration records to reflect build of the devices. 
 
 
 Develop change documentation for subsequent approval by client agencies. 
 
 
 Commission routers and network monitoring hardware within the PSN remotely in conjunction with contracted installers on site. 
 
 
 Update inventory and configuration records to reflect commissioning of the new devices and removal of the previous devices. 
 
 
 Conduct data integrity checks for hardware and PSN sites. 
 
 
 Conduct handovers of hardware to the Operations team for ongoing support and maintenance. 
 
 
 Operate within PSNMC technical framework for Change, Release, Incident and Problem Management processes. 
 
 
   What you'll need to succeed  
 To thrive in this role, you will need to demonstrate the following: 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with SR-MPLS networks. 
 
 
 Demonstrated understanding of overlay and underlay layer 3 routing protocols including MP-BGP and OSPF and experience in environments with hundreds of individual peering's using IPv4 and IPv6. 
 
 
 Demonstrated understanding of end to end Quality of Service (QoS) deployment regime incorporating: o MPLS QoS 
 
 
 o Layer 3 QoS in a non-MPLS environment 
 o Layer 2 QoS in a non-MPLS environment 
 
 
 Familiarity with Cisco routers. 
 
 
 Familiarity with Network Virtualisation Technologies e.g. MPLS VPNs including: VRFs, VPLS, EVPN, VRF-lite and VXLAN. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with wireless and radio networks, such as controller, access point, WLAN, 4/5G LTE design and deployment using Cisco. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience managing authentication technologies such as TACACS, Radius, OTP, Active Directory, SAML / SSO and OAuth. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with remote access and encryption technologies for site to site (e.g. IPSEC VPNs, Cisco DMVPN) and client to site (e.g. SSL VPN) Always On VPN, and MACsec. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience analysing packet captures and logs to determine application and network issues using tcpdump, Wireshark, NetScout and Splunk tools. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with carrier core, aggregation, access interconnect such as PNI, NNI and subscriber access. Retail and wholesale telecommunications service mapping and hand-off. 
 
 
     
  What you'll get in return  
 
 By joining the Queensland Government, you are joining a dynamic team committed to shaping and elevating Queensland's workforce to meet the evolving needs of our industries, ensuring prosperity and agility in our economic landscape.

 A career with the department means making a real difference - join us in building a skilled, adaptable, and vibrant workforce for Queensland.

 Role Overview 
 We are seeking a motivated and physically fit  Pick Packer / Warehouse Operator  to join our team. In this busy, hands-on role, you will be responsible for accurate order picking, operating material handling equipment (tugger), packing, and staging orders for dispatch using RF scanners, computer systems for shipping labels, and pallet wrap machines. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 
 
  Order Picking & Equipment Operation:  
 
 
 Safe operation of an electric tugger pulling pallets throughout the warehouse. 
 
 
 Accurately pick items from shelving (up to 1.6 metres high) using an RF scanner and place them onto pallets. 
 
 
 Safely open incoming wrapped pallets using utility knives as required. 
 
 
 
 
  Packing, Scanning & Dispatch Prep:  
 
 
 Transport picked orders to the packing desk. 
 
 
 Scan items into the system and use a desktop PC interface to generate and print accurate shipping labels. 
 
 
 Apply labels directly to the relevant items/cartons. 
 
 
 
 
  Pallet Wrapping & Staging:  
 
 
 Transport completed pallets to the stretch wrap station and operate the pallet wrapping machine. 
 
 
 Use the tugger to transport fully wrapped, labelled pallets to the designated staging area for transport pickup. 
 
 
 Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free workstation. 
 
 
 
 
 Required Skills & Experience 
 
 
  Experience:  Previous experience in a warehouse, pick-packing, or logistics environment (RF scanning experience or tugger operation is a plus). 
 
 
  Technical Skills:  Basic computer literacy to navigate label printing software and scan items accurately. 
 
 
  Physical Capability:  Comfortable standing, walking, and reaching up to 1.6m height during shift operations. 
 
 
  Personal Attributes:  High attention to detail, punctuality, and the ability to work productively in a busy environment.

We care for thousands of children each year in our hospitals and in their homes with one purpose in mind - to help young people live their healthiest lives. **This position is available for the current clinical year, up to 31 January 2027 only**

The 0.5 FTE Clinical Ethics Provisional Fellowship at The Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN) is available to commence as soon as possible up to 31 January 2027. This position is an advanced training position in Clinical Ethics. The Fellow will help provide input and participate in further developing the SCHN Clinical Ethics Support Service (CESS) which is acknowledged as an important service within the Network. The Fellowship is a valuable learning experience both for the Fellow and the Network, in developing and sharing ethics capacity at all organisational levels, and reflecting on 'what we ought to do, not just what we can do' in clinical care. 

The Fellow will be involved in all five domains of the SCHN CESS: education, clinical ethics consultation, embedding ethics into organisational policy, research and academic connections and clinical ethics service planning and development. The fellow will assist in planning and scheduling Clinical Ethics meetings and forums and participate in education, service delivery and research with support from the Clinical Ethicist and Clinical Ethics Medical Lead. Advanced training in bioethics is currently offered via universities as a Graduate Diploma, Graduate Certificate, Master's degree or PhD studies, all of which require major commitment of time and money. 

This Network role involves dividing time equitably and attending activities and meetings at both The Children's Hospital at Westmead (CHW), and Sydney Children's Hospital, Randwick (SCH). The Fellowship offers an invaluable opportunity to gain experience and training in Clinical Ethics. The Fellow will also contribute to the important development of the SCHN Clinical Ethics Support Service. 
 

Please refer to the position description and contact person for further information about the position.

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia in an appropriate registration category.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Excellent communication, leadership and teamwork skills with demonstrated ability to liaise effectively with other health professionals.

Ongoing commitment to further education and professional development and demonstrated ability to teach, with a willingness to participate in the teaching of Medical Students, Junior Medical Staff and other clinical staff.

Understanding of research methodology or research experience and a willingness to undertake research proposal.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent time management, problem solving skills, clinical skills, judgment and expertise.

Grow your specialty nursing career on the Central Coast.

The Transition to Specialty Practice (TSP) Program is a 12-month program offering Registered Nurses the opportunity to develop specialised knowledge and skills through a structured program of education, clinical experience, mentorship and professional development. Offered across a broad range of nursing specialties, the program builds the capability to provide evidence-based care across acute and specialised settings.

Working alongside experienced clinicians, educators and multidisciplinary teams, participants are supported to develop confidence, refine clinical judgement and strengthen advanced clinical assessment, critical thinking and care coordination skills.

Whether you are looking to expand your clinical expertise, transition into a new specialty, or build a long-term career pathway, the program provides a supportive pathway to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence required to deliver exceptional care.

We are recruiting across twelve specialties on the Central Coast for 2027. Explore each below and apply for the one that fits where you want your nursing career to go.

Aged Care & Subacute
 Build expertise in complex aged care, dementia and delirium, rehabilitation, wound care, chronic disease and end-of-life care. Develop advanced clinical skills while delivering person-centred care that promotes independence, recovery and quality of life.

Acute Community Mental Health
Discover a career in Community Mental Health Nursing, supporting people to achieve recovery, resilience and independence. Develop skills in mental health assessment, therapeutic engagement, care coordination and crisis intervention while delivering recovery-focused, trauma-informed and person-centred care.

Community Nursing
Take your nursing career beyond the hospital walls and make a difference where people live, recover and thrive. Build skills in community-based care, chronic disease management, hospital avoidance, rehabilitation and palliative care, while supporting independence and better health outcomes closer to home.

Gastroenterology
Build specialised skills in managing complex acute and chronic gastrointestinal conditions, liver disease, nutrition and symptom management. Strengthen your clinical assessment and decision-making while supporting patients through diagnosis, treatment and recovery.

General Medicine & MAU 
Thrive in a fast-paced acute medical environment, building expertise in rapid assessment, clinical reasoning and recognising patient deterioration. Develop the skills and confidence to manage diverse and complex medical presentations while delivering timely, coordinated patient care.

Intensive Care
Step into the world of critical care and develop advanced skills in life-support therapies, mechanical ventilation, haemodynamic monitoring and rapid patient deterioration. Build your confidence and critical thinking while caring for some of the most complex and critically ill patients.

Neurology
Discover the complexity of Neurology Nursing and build expertise in stroke, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy and neurodegenerative conditions. Develop advanced neurological assessment, critical thinking and clinical decision-making skills while supporting patients across acute and ongoing care.

Oncology & Haematology
Discover a specialty where clinical expertise, compassion and human connection come together. Build specialist skills in cancer therapies, complex assessment, symptom management, supportive care and oncological emergencies, supporting patients and families throughout their cancer journey.

Paediatric
Make a meaningful difference in the lives of children, young people and their families. Develop specialised skills in paediatric assessment, recognising deterioration and family-centred care, supporting children across acute, chronic and complex health conditions.

Perioperative
Discover a career where precision, teamwork and patient care come together. Develop specialised skills in Scrub-Scout and Recovery Nursing, building expertise in surgical safety, aseptic technique, airway management and post-operative care.

Renal
Explore a specialty where advanced clinical care, technical expertise and meaningful patient relationships come together. Develop specialised skills in dialysis therapies, acute and chronic kidney disease, fluid and electrolyte management and complex renal care.

Respiratory
Discover a specialty where every breath makes a difference. Develop expertise in acute and chronic respiratory care, respiratory distress, oxygen therapies and non-invasive ventilation, while building advanced assessment and clinical deterioration skills.

'NETS', The Newborn & paediatric Emergency Transport Service, is a statewide service of NSW Health, hosted by The Sydney Children's Hospitals Network. It is the only service of its kind in Australia; providing expert clinical advice, clinical co-ordination, emergency treatment and stabilisation and inter-hospital transport for very sick or injured babies and children up to the age of 16 years. NETS operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Of some 6,785 calls received per year, 3,994 are transported by NETS teams by road or air. Our teams travel via road, rotary and fixed wing. 

NETS is also a referral service, providing a forum for clinical triage for patients too sick for normal ambulance transfer between hospitals. NETS connects clinicians in referring and receiving hospitals in a telephone conference to discuss the best treatment and appropriateness of transfer or retrieval. 

The Advanced Trainee is responsible for the delivery of the highest quality care to the paediatric patient and their family. Referring hospitals expect knowledge, skills and competencies which may exceed those available in the referring hospital. A high level of competency in assessment, treatment and procedural skills (such as cannulation, high level airway skills, chest tube thoracostomy, central line placement) is expected prior to employment. The care that is delivered should be individual and continually reviewed. The Advanced Trainee should be an active clinical resource contributing towards continuing education for themselves and their peers.

About the Monash Health Pathology Service 






The Monash Health Pathology Service operates under the brand name Monash Pathology and is an integral part of Monash. It is the largest provider of Pathology services in the State of Victoria and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these is located at the Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional facilities being located at the Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection centres based within the hospital sites and community settings. Services are provided to the Public and Private sectors, and other laboratory services.

Join our team as a Medical Scientist (Cytogenetics) Grade 1 in a full time, ongoing role to work at Monash Health Pathology based at Clayton. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the Principal Scientist, Senior Scientists, Pathologists and working with the broader Diagnostic Genomics Laboratory team. 






The Diagnostic Genomics Laboratory, Monash Pathology is made up of three different areas which operates a Monday to Friday service 8am to 5pm: 







The Cytogenetics Laboratory which processes a range of prenatal and postnatal specimens, using conventional and molecular diagnostic techniques. This includes DNA extraction, tissue culture, FISH, Microarray and Karyotyping. 


The Genetics and Molecular Pathology laboratory which provides a specialised genetic testing service for oncology, haematology as well as inherited diseases. Our genomics team currently offers DNA and RNA next generation sequencing (NGS) for targeted panels in solid tumour biology, haematology and cardiac. The Thalassaemia and Haemophilia Molecular laboratory's role is to confirm the genetic basis for thalassaemia and other significant haemoglobinopathies, identify carrier status and perform prenatal testing for couples at risk of giving birth to children with severe disease. Proven experience in a diagnostic laboratory setting with strong technical capabilities and commitment to quality outcomes. 


Prior experience with molecular techniques in a NATA accredited laboratory such as DNA extraction, PCR, karyotyping, microarray and-or FISH is highly desirable.








Mandatory requirements of the role - qualifications:







Degree in Science or Applied Science (MLS) or recognised equivalent plus the appropriate laboratory experience. 


Post graduate qualification or studying for a post graduate qualification is desirable

Salary packaging.

Trainees complete Basic Training over three years (36 months full time equivalent) guided by the Basic Training handbooks and curricula in Paediatrics & Child Health. The Divisional Written Examination and Divisional Clinical Examination is towards the end of training to test a trainee's knowledge and skills and determine if they are eligible to progress to Advanced Training.

The vision for South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD) is 'exceptional care, healthier lives'. SESLHD is committed to enabling our community to be healthy and well, and to providing the best possible compassionate care when people need it.

This six-month rotation-contract may commence from 1 February 2027 (Term 1) or 2 August 2027 (Term 3) per preference and training requirements of the successful candidate(s).

About our Role

The Prince of Wales Emergency Department offers an ACEM-accredited six-month Emergency Medicine Ultrasound Special Skills Placement (SSP) for Stage 2-4 trainees. The position is full-time, comprising 0.5 FTE protected ultrasound training and 0.5 FTE clinical Emergency Medicine, providing trainees with the opportunity to develop expertise in both the technical and clinical application of point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS). The placement also offers experience in ultrasound-guided procedures while encouraging participation in education, quality improvement, and research within a supportive, multidisciplinary teaching environment.

Our program includes:

Credentialing in core and extended PoCUS modules in accordance with ACEM and-or ASUM standards.
Individualised supervision and mentoring by two Clinical Leads in Ultrasound (CLUS), both with extensive US experience across FELS, lung, eFAST, abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), renal, proximal DVT, early pregnancy, hepatobiliary as well as ultrasound-guided procedures.

Support with ASUM CCPU accreditation, including mentorship from an ASUM CCPU logbook reviewer, providing guidance with image acquisition, logbook development and credentialing requirements.

Protected one-to-one scanning sessions with Sonographer Educators in the Emergency Department (SEEDs), comprising dedicated cardiac and general sonographers.

Early pregnancy ultrasound experience through exposure to the Early Pregnancy Assessment Service (EPAS) at the Royal Hospital for Women.

Development as a PoCUS Educator, with opportunities to lead JMO teaching on peripheral IVcannulation, instruct on PoCUS courses and training sessions, and present cases at the biannual Joint Hospitals Ultrasound Meetings.

Research and quality improvement opportunities, including audit, educational resource development, protocol and guideline development, and contributions to the departmental PoCUS newsletter.

Regional anaesthesia experience, including ultrasound-guided nerve blocks and multidisciplinaryteaching with the Anaesthetics and Acute Pain Service.

Multidisciplinary collaboration with Intensive Care, including attendance at dedicated echocardiography teaching sessions and shared educational activities.

 

Our Primary Location

Prince of Wales Hospital and Community Health Services is a major teaching hospital and tertiary referral centre based on the Randwick Hospitals Campus. We provide excellent healthcare to SESLHD and specialist health and medical services to NSW. We connect with various universities including the University of New South Wales. Our premier medical facilities enable leading learning opportunities for our staff, with the Randwick Campus Redevelopment providing a world-class integrated environment for clinical care, research and education.

We have 450 inpatient beds and almost 3,000 staff. Each year we care for more than 64,000 patients in our Emergency Department and around 50,000 patients are admitted to our Hospital. We also have a busy outpatient service and rural outreach service and provide more than 900,000 occasions of non-admitted patient care each year.

Randwick is a metropolitan hub in Sydney's Eastern Suburbs. We have a vibrant, multicultural community, with diverse dining options and regular entertainment hosted by our local council. For those fond of coastal living, we are a walk away from Coogee Beach. A short drive takes you to the famous Bondi Beach and Centennial Parklands. Cycling paths and public transport are readily available, with Sydney's light rail connecting the campus to Sydney's CBD just 7 kilometres away.

Come enjoy a blend of urban convenience and relaxed coastal living at Randwick and:

Four weeks of annual leave + an extra Allocated Day Off (ADO) per month.

Other leave including parental leave, FACS leave, and study & education leave.

Salary Packaging, a way to pay for certain items with your pre-tax salary.

Quality learning and development, research opportunities, and more.
